suitability_reason: Dependency/HOH/CTC/EITC outcomes follow from relationship (no marriage found), full-year-household test, and EITC no-child phaseout threshold; marriage finding is factual but the downstream tests are mechanical.

taxpayer.notes: Resided in Missouri when petition filed; California resident/domiciliary until mid-March 2016. Claimed common law marriage in Kansas (2011) to mother of the two children; court found no marriage.

adjustments: disallowed dependency exemptions for A.D.B. and J.N.B.
disallowed head of household filing status
disallowed child tax credit (including additional child tax credit)
IRS froze $7,572 of the claimed refund
notice_of_deficiency.contested_by_taxpayer: Claims children are his stepchildren via a 2011 Kansas common law marriage to their mother, entitling him to exemptions, HOH, CTC/ACTC, and EITC.
conceded: Respondent conceded the section 6662(a) accuracy-related penalty

findings_of_fact.fact: Petitioner is not the biological or adoptive father of A.D.B. and J.N.B.; Daniela is their mother
findings_of_fact.snippet: Daniela Bourne4 is the mother of A.D.B. and J.N.B. Mr. Brzyski is not the biological or adoptive father of those children.

findings_of_fact.fact: Court finds petitioner was not married to Daniela in 2016 (no Kansas common law marriage proven); so children are not stepchildren
findings_of_fact.snippet: whether Mr. Brzyski was married to Daniela in 2016. We find he was not.

findings_of_fact.fact: Neither California nor Missouri allows common law marriage
findings_of_fact.snippet: Neither California nor Missouri allows for common law marriage; therefore, Mr. Brzyski had to form the common law marriage in Kansas.

findings_of_fact.fact: In 2016 A.D.B. was age 7 and J.N.B. was age 11
findings_of_fact.snippet: In 2016 A.D.B. was age 7 and J.N.B. was age 11.

findings_of_fact.fact: The children did not reside with petitioner for the full 12 months of 2016
findings_of_fact.snippet: The children did not reside with Mr. Brzyski for the full 12 months of2016.

findings_of_fact.fact: Petitioner resided in California until mid-March 2016, then moved to Missouri living with his mother until October 2016; children lived in California through the 2015-16 school year and moved to Missouri between June and October 2016
findings_of_fact.snippet: The children left California and started living in Missouri sometime between June and October 2016.

findings_of_fact.fact: No documentation that petitioner provided over half of children's support
findings_of_fact.snippet: Because Mr. Brzyski could not substantiate his financial support of the children, we find that he does not meet the financial support requirement.
have less gross income than the section 151(d) exemption amount ($4,050 for 2016)

findings_of_fact.fact: Petitioner's 2016 earned income was $16,788 (greater than AGI); claimed refund $9,288
findings_of_fact.snippet: The return reported earned income of $16,788 and claimed a refund of $9,288.

findings_of_fact.fact: 2016 completed phaseout amount for EITC with no qualifying children (single) is $14,880
findings_of_fact.snippet: For 2016, the completed phaseout amount for single filers is listed as $14,880.

findings_of_fact.fact: Children were also claimed as dependents on their maternal grandfather's 2016 return
findings_of_fact.snippet: The children were also claimed as dependents on the grandfather's 2016 return.

issues.question: Is petitioner entitled to dependency exemptions for A.D.B. and J.N.B. for 2016?
issues.holding: No. Not qualifying children: no relationship (not biological/adoptive/stepparent since not married). Not qualifying relatives: did not live with him the entire year (152(d)(2)(H)) and support test not substantiated.
issues.computable_reason: Given found facts (no marriage, no full-year household membership), relationship tests fail mechanically; marriage finding itself was factual.

issues.question: Is petitioner entitled to head of household filing status for 2016?
issues.holding: No; he has no dependent under section 151 or qualifying child under 152(c).
issues.computable_reason: Follows mechanically from absence of qualifying child/dependent.

issues.question: Is petitioner entitled to the child tax credit and additional child tax credit for 2016?
issues.holding: No; children are not his qualifying children under 152(c).
issues.computable_reason: Follows from failure of 152(c) relationship test.

issues.question: Is petitioner entitled to the earned income tax credit for 2016?
issues.holding: No; no qualifying children, and earned income $16,788 exceeds the $14,880 no-child completed phaseout amount.

amount_determined.description: earned income compared to completed phaseout amount

decision.text: Decision will be entered for respondent as to the deficiency and for petitioner as to the accuracy-related penalty under section 6662(a).
decision.summary: $7,816 deficiency sustained; no exemptions, HOH, CTC/ACTC or EITC; 6662(a) penalty conceded by respondent.

notes: Some facts stipulated. Burden on petitioner; no 7491(a) shift. Penalty conceded (footnote 2), so not an issue. Opinion cites $14,880 as completed phaseout for single filers with no qualifying children; footnote cites both Rev. Proc. 2015-53 and 2016-53. Common law marriage is a state-law fact question decided on credibility (Kansas law). The 2016 amended MFJ return was not accepted/processed.
